data.description:
# Audit Stuck in `in_progress` When `run-release` is Aborted

## Problem Statement

When the `run-release` script is aborted (e.g., via Ctrl+C or signal) while the audit gate is running audits on work items, those items are left stuck in the `in_progress` state. The audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` claim is performed before the try/finally block in `cmd_issue` can catch the abort, and a hard kill (SIGKILL) bypasses Python's finally blocks entirely. This breaks the release pipeline because items stuck in `in_progress` are excluded from the `in_review` candidate query.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Runs `run-release` and needs the pipeline to complete or abort cleanly without manual work-item intervention.
- **Automated agents**: Agents waiting for work items to reach `in_review` stage to proceed with release gating.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit runner restores pre-audit status on hard abort**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGKILL (signal 9) during an audit, it must still restore the work item to its pre-audit state (`completed`/`in_review` or whatever it was before the audit). Since Python cannot catch SIGKILL, the solution must use a subprocess wrapper or a separate watchdog process that observes the audit child's death and restores the captured pre-audit status.
- **AC2 — Audit runner restores status on SIGTERM/SIGINT**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the status restoration must still complete even if killed mid-try-block. Python's default SIGINT handling raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, so the `finally` block in `cmd_issue` covers SIGINT, but the default SIGTERM disposition terminates the process *without* running `finally` blocks. An explicit `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handler that performs the cleanup and then re-raises (or restores the default disposition and re-signals) is therefore required for SIGTERM.
- **AC3 — No `in_progress` items left after any abort scenario**: After any termination of `audit_runner.py` (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL, or process death), the audited work item must NOT remain in `in_progress` state. This can be verified by checking the work item's status after a forced kill.
- **AC4 — All existing audit tests pass**: The fix must not break any existing audit tests in `skill/audit/tests/`.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce new race conditions in concurrent audit scenarios (multiple `audit_runner.py` processes auditing the same or different items).
- The solution must follow existing project conventions: no direct `wl update` outside the audit runner's lifecycle management.
- If a direct Python-level SIGKILL handler is impossible, a wrapper mechanism (e.g., a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death) must be used.

## Existing State

- The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `in_progress` status in `_phase_gate` (the `wl update ... --status in_progress` claim is issued at `audit_runner.py:8219`; `_phase_gate` starts at line 7938) before entering the main `try/finally` block in `cmd_issue`.
- The `finally` block in `cmd_issue` calls `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` which restores the pre-audit state.
- `check-audit-gate.js` (used by `run-release.js`) invokes `audit_runner.py issue <id>` via `execSync` for each candidate work item.
- When the `run-release` script is aborted, the `execSync` call is terminated, killing the `audit_runner.py` child process.
- If killed with SIGKILL (signal 9), Python's `finally` blocks do not execute, leaving the item in `in_progress`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Needs a signal handling mechanism or wrapper to ensure status restoration on hard abort.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — May need a timeout/abort handler to clean up on termination.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New tests for abort scenarios.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQRZ5N6005WI43**: [test-failure] test-check-audit-gate.mjs / test-close-work-items.mjs / test-run-release.mjs (6 node failures) — failing test (still open, critical priority)
- **SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB**: Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status — uses trap/finally pattern for exit cleanup (relevant pattern to follow)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Is the abort specifically SIGKILL, or does SIGTERM also fail to restore status?" — Answer (Map): SIGTERM should be handled by Python's finally blocks, but SIGKILL cannot be caught by Python at all. The fix must handle SIGKILL via a wrapper mechanism. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Can a wrapper process approach work here?" — Answer (Map): Yes, a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death is an acceptable approach. Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Audit stuck in in_progress when run-release is aborted

data.description:
## Context
The standup skill currently writes to stdout by default and only writes to a file when --output-path is supplied. The desired UX is to default to a dated file under ./standups/ so reports accumulate without manual path management.

## Goal
As an operator I want `python3 $(skill_path standup)/scripts/generate_standup.py` to write its report to `./standups/<year>_<month>_<day>.md` by default so that daily standup reports are persisted automatically.

## Work
- Change the default behaviour of `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` so that when `--output-path` is NOT provided it writes the rendered report to `./standups/<YYYY>_<MM>_<DD>.md` relative to the project root (the worklog's parent dir when --worklog-dir / WL_WORKLOG_DIR is set, otherwise cwd / cwd resolution).
- Ensure the target directory is created if it does not exist.
- Preserve explicit `--output-path <path>` override (when supplied, that path is used unchanged).
- Update `skill/standup/SKILL.md` Invocation docs to reflect the new default.
- Handle date as the report generation date (local datetime at generation time) formatted as zero-padded YYYY_MM_DD (e.g. 2026_09_10.md).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Running without --output-path writes a markdown report to ./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md (e.g. ./standups/2026_09_10.md) using the current local date, creating ./standups/ if needed. (verified: manual smoke + test_default_path_writes_markdown_and_creates_dir)
- [x] Running with --output-path <path> still writes to that explicit path and does not also write to the default dated path. (verified: manual smoke + test_explicit_output_path_used_instead_of_default)
- [x] SKILL.md documents the new default ("./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md" when --output-path omitted).
- [x] Existing flags (--json, --verbose, --worklog-dir, --count, --startTime, --duration) continue to work. (all 9 pre-existing standup tests pass unmodified; --json covered in new tests)
- [x] Tests cover both the default dated file path and the --output-path override. (8 new tests in test_generate_standup_default_output_path.py)

## Out of scope
- Changing the report contents/format beyond routing the output destination.

data.comment: Resuming after audit rejection. Audit base cae176e4 flagged AC4 partial: --json without --output-path wrote a JSON artifact into the default dated .md file, breaking the documented '--json # Fetch data' stdout contract (SKILL.md:116). Root cause: the default-output-path change applied unconditionally to both output formats. Fix (TDD): replaced test_default_json_writes_json_to_standups_dated_file with test_default_json_streams_to_stdout_without_dated_file (red first), then main() now streams JSON to stdout when --json is set without --output-path, writes the default dated .md only for the rendered markdown report, and keeps --output-path override for either format. Updated script docstring + SKILL.md --json/--output-path rows. All code-quality findings from the audit base (orig_wl/rc F841, ruff findings) were already fixed on dev after the audit; ruff on skill/standup/ is clean. Smoke-verified all three modes.
